_about: Fire agents, burning and barrel bombs, DECODED from the original rather than
taken from the Godot project's hazards.json, which marks all three _guess and gets
every one of them wrong. Fire.hpp cites the byte offsets.
Constants inside the original pass through SGlobalScale::scale() before they
are used. The port's view is 256 px tall and scaleFactor is screenSize.y/256,
so one scale unit is one port pixel and these are written as plain pixels.
That is said once here rather than against each number.

_note: A fire agent tests squaredDistance(other, self) < size.x * size.x, so this
is a RADIUS and the test is centre to centre, not shape against shape.
size.x is GetSize().x, the sprite's frame times its scale: fire_agent.png is
32 x 32 with SpriteCut 1 x 1 and Scale 1.0. ETHSpriteEntity::GetCurrentSize
is what GetSize registers to, and the engine hands it to IsPointOnSprite as
the sprite's extent; GetCollisionBox is a separate method.
The Godot project reads the .ent's 38 x 38 <Collision> instead and halves it to 24
(hazards.json _guess). That box is not what GetSize returns, and the entity's
shape is 0 - it has no physics body at all.
_burn_projectile: A fire agent's fourth branch turns a flying projectile.ent into a fireball (planning
GetPositionXY and its 'direction', #22-27 killProjectile (a bare DeleteEntity), #29-46
addFireball(point, direction, false, 1) - killMainCharacter clear. The agent is static
and runs after the shot, which deletes itself on the frame it passes the end of its way
(ETHCallback_projectile #127-156, #265-270), so only a shot still in flight is burned.
The port tests it on the shot's way (Portals::Flame, at reach_px) and Game makes the
fireball (turrets.json's speed and radius). Its launch sound, addFireball's
playFireballSound, is not played, as it is not for the fire diamond's conversion: the
audio audit's row 16, the sound pass (P6).
_burn_minion: The second branch, burn() on what is burnable and not burned (#193-220), reaches a
minion too: minion.ent and ghost_minion.ent carry burnable 1, and a minion is not a
character (isCharacter is set by GameCharacter's constructor alone), so a flame only
sets its `burned`. The minion is dynamic and its callback runs before the static
agent's, so it destroys itself on the NEXT frame (ETHCallback_minion #1456-1471) and

_note: BURN_TIME, the global the carranca script sets to 1000. A burning crate
fades to black and to nothing over this time and is then removed; the
removal is the puzzle, since burning a crate deletes a platform or a
blocker. The Godot project invents 2000 and marks it _guess.
fade_names is the whole of it: burn() only sets the `burned` flag, and the
fade-and-remove lives in manageBurnable, whose ONE caller is crateCallback.
A shock_agent carries metadata/burnable too (levels 2-12, 2-14, 2-19) and
merely holds the flag when lit - it does not fade and is not removed. Every
crate spelling the 128 levels place is listed; the original writes the same
logical crate both bare and with .ent, and those are different entities.
explode builds an EntityGrabber of radius 80 and tests it against each
candidate's REAL collider - circle against circle, or sphere against a box
in the box's own frame - skipping anything with no physics body. The Godot project
invents 96 and marks it _guess.
kills_player is FALSE and that is the original's own answer, not a
simplification. The grabber's filter is isBreakableOrExplosiveOrBurnable,
which does not include characters, and no main_char placement carries any of
those three flags - so although barrel_bomb passes killPlayer true, the
player is never in the grabbed set. Fire kills the player; a blast does not.
test_mp_fire pins both directions, because this is the kind of asymmetry a
port smooths away without noticing.
_breakables_in_a_blast: explode also sets `destroy` on every entity it grabs (#111-122). Fire reports what
each blast reached with a clear line and Demolish, the one owner of a breakable's
breaking, takes the breakable walls away on the same tick: demolish.json `blast`

_source: to the entity by name (ETHCallback_ + RemoveExtension, ETHASUtil.cpp:63-67, so both
spellings: 00_order 8.0 rule 4), runs for whatever begins a contact with it: #1-11
GetUInt('burnable') of the other, #12-19 burn(other) when it is not 0; then #21-30
SetUInt('explode', 1) on the other, unconditionally. Nothing else: no character's hp
is touched, so the lava kills nobody (level31c's player dies of the level's edge,
hazards.json bounds, at y 352, 46 u above the lava's top). A barrel's own callback
(ETHCallback_barrel_bomb #31-60) reads `explode` and blasts, so a barrel that falls
into the lava goes off there. One lava in the game: level31c's lava_1140, a solid
768 x 128 box at (384, 462) (the converter's StaticBody2D: sensor 0).
_margin_note: How near a body must come to the lava's box to touch it. The solver leaves a body
resting on a floor touching it rather than overlapping it, so the port's overlap
test grows the box by this much, as demolish.json's contact.margin_px does for a
stone. A threshold of the port's, not a measurement.
